evidence: From Waiohine Road End and Campsite, cross the high suspension bridge over the Waiohine River.
If you are going to Cone Saddle rather than Cone Hut, continue along the main ridge track.
The track descends gently before reaching Cone Saddle at 566 m.

evidence: Approximately halfway between the 682 high point and Cone Saddle, you will come to another track junction.
Here you have the option to take the left hand track and descend steeply to Cone Hut.
It is around 1 km down this track to Cone Hut, which is situated on a pretty terrace above the Tauwharenīkau River.

evidence: From Cone Saddle, the track climbs steadily to Mount Cone, gaining around 500 m in elevation.
To go to Totara Flats Hut, take the right hand track that continues straight ahead along the ridge.
The track emerges onto a river terrace not far upstream from Totara Flats Hut.
The hut is a few minutes downstream from the bridge.

evidence: From Totara Flats Hut, follow the track upstream.
Follow the track along Cone Ridge, until you come to a track junction.
Take the right hand track to Neill Forks Hut.
After the second Neill Creek crossing, you come to Neill Forks Hut, near the confluence of Hector River and Neill Creek.

doubts: This page describes several tracks around Cone Ridge as separate legs, so it is a network; W1 is taken as main only because it comes first. Waiohine Road End has no road-end feature in the packet, so W1 and W2 starts have no ref. The page does not say whether walkers return the same way; each leg is recorded as one_way only because it is described from A to B. W2 (to Cone Hut) is the option offered under the same heading 'Waiohine Road End to Cone Hut/Cone Saddle' and has no separate time. Huts lists the huts on all the described ways (none is on W1 itself). The Cone Saddle to Cone Hut or Waiohine Valley tracks are covered on the Holdsworth-Kaitoke Track page. Map tracks T1 (Cone Saddle Track) and T2 (Tauwharenikau Track) are not named in the text, so they are not used.
